result.summary:
Text filters (string, text, search) whose operator splits the value into search terms now show a warning when the value has more than 5 terms. The tokenizer keeps at most 5 terms (MAX_TOKENS) and reports truncated?. Query#filter_warnings returns one message per truncated filter. The warnings render as

above the results in the issue list, time entry list and report, calendar and Gantt chart, with the terms HTML-escaped. Results are still shown and the query stays valid. check-fast and the full check both pass (no failures, lint clean). Nothing was committed. A dated entry was added to docs/harness/log.md, as AGENTS.md asks.

changes.summary: Tokenizer: MAX_TOKENS = 5 constant, tokens returns at most MAX_TOKENS, new truncated? (true when more than MAX_TOKENS terms), the term list is memoized in a private all_tokens.

TERMS_OPERATORS (~, *~, !~, ^, $) and TERMS_FILTER_TYPES (string, text, search) constants; new filter_warnings returns one localized message per truncated filter, using the filter label, the max, and the quoted terms joined with support.array.words_connector.

New render_query_filter_warnings(query) that renders each warning as

(content_tag escapes the text).
Renders the filter warnings above the results.
Renders the filter warnings above the results.
Renders the filter warnings above the results (same query form as the time entry list).
Renders the filter warnings after the query errors, above the chart.
Renders the filter warnings after the query errors, above the calendar.
Adds notice_query_search_terms_truncated: "%{label}: A maximum of %{max} search terms can be used. Only the following terms were used: %{terms}".
Tokenizer tests: max tokens and truncated?, no truncation at 5 terms, ignored terms and duplicates do not count.
filter_warnings tests: exact message and results still returned, one warning per truncated filter, no warning at 5 terms, no warning for non-splitting operators.
Helper tests: warnings are rendered as escaped p.warning, nothing rendered without warnings.
Issue list with 6 terms shows the warning and the matching issue.
Gantt with 6 terms shows the warning and the chart.
Calendar with 6 terms shows the warning and the calendar.
Dated entry for the change: what changed, what was learned, what is left.

acceptance.criterion: A filter value with more than 5 terms shows the warning and the results
acceptance.evidence: Functional tests: issues index (p.warning with the 5-term message, and a[href="/issues/1"] still listed), gantt and calendar (p.warning matches and the chart/calendar renders). All pass.

acceptance.criterion: The change is covered by tests
acceptance.evidence: Tokenizer tests (search_test.rb), filter_warnings tests (query_test.rb), helper escaping test (queries_helper_test.rb), and functional tests for issues, gantt and calendar (issues_controller_test.rb, gantts_controller_test.rb, calendars_controller_test.rb). Targeted run: 14 runs, 0 failures before the gantt/calendar additions; those 3 also pass.

acceptance.evidence: bin/harness check-fast: 3257 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors, 48 skips, lint ok (exit 0). bin/harness check: 1099 files no offenses, 6072 runs, 31676 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 64 skips (exit 0). System tests were not run (need Chrome), as the project's full gate excludes them.

harness_gaps.problem: Single-file test commands (bin/rails test ...) fail with the default macOS Ruby 2.6 (Bundler lockfile error) and only work when a Ruby 3.3 to 4.0 is first on PATH. bin/harness picks a Ruby, but it is not documented that bin/rails needs the same PATH. I had to prepend /opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin.
The docs do not say which Ruby the gates need on a Mac with the system Ruby; docs/harness/log.md mentions Homebrew Ruby 4.0 but the single-test command in AGENTS.md does not.
